newsitem.title: MALI: Malian Segala gold mine sees higher deposit.
newsitem.headline: Malian Segala gold mine sees higher deposit.

text.p: Mali's Segala mine could double its gold deposit estimate to two million ounces as revisions to an earlier feasibility study in 1995 near completion, minority owners Consolidated Mining Corporation West Africa told Reuters.

"At this stage of the studies we can say that the first estimations could be multiplied by two, going from one to two million ounces," CMCWA chairman Amadou Toure said in an interview, adding that the estimate had not been finalised.
Feasibility studies by Canada-based Oliver Gold at Segala -- 29 percent-owned by private Malian firm CMCWA -- could lead to mine construction in 1998 at a cost of $110 million, he said.
The latest estimate has not yet been officially announced in Mali.

Canada-based Trillion Ressources Limited holds a 51 percent majority stake in CMCWA. Another 29 percent is owned by Consolidated Mining Company (South Africa) and 20 percent by private Malian shareholders.
"We are in discussions with several partners," Toure said, adding that finance would be sought "through Canadian, American financial markets or even through London banks."
The mine would be able to process 1.82 million tonnes a year of ore containing 2.8 grammes/tonne of gold. It would employ 220 staff.
Segala, discovered in 1984, covers eight square kilometres of western Mali's ore-rich Kenieba region.
